Let’s dive into Chapter 4: Building Confidence and Embracing Strategic Risk-Taking.
By now, as you’ve become more aware of your own habits and the world around you, the next step is all about building up the confidence you need to take smart, strategic risks.
Here’s something you might relate to—so many women hold back from chasing new opportunities, negotiating for better terms, or stepping into leadership roles. Why? Often, it’s because of self-doubt or that nagging fear of failure.
But guess what? Breaking through those barriers starts with a shift in how you think, and a willingness to push beyond what feels comfortable.
Confidence isn’t something you’re born with—it’s a skill you can build, little by little, through practice and real-world experience. It starts by noticing and challenging your inner critic—that voice inside that questions if you’re good enough or deserving enough.
So often, this inner narrative just repeats what society says is possible for us. But just because you think it, doesn’t mean it’s true.
One powerful way to grow your confidence is to see mistakes and setbacks differently. Instead of proof that you’re not cut out for something, what if you treated them as stepping stones—valuable chances to learn and get better?
In plenty of workplaces, it’s the folks who take smart risks and bounce back from failure who really stand out for their initiative and resilience.
On the flip side, playing it safe all the time? That can mean missing out on growth, recognition, and new challenges.
Think about this: imagine someone who hesitates to apply for a promotion just because she doesn’t check every single box on the job description. Meanwhile, others—maybe with less experience or fewer credentials—put their names forward and get a shot.
Most of the time, what sets people apart isn’t their ability—it’s their willingness to take a chance and speak up for themselves.
If you’re ready to boost your confidence and start taking more strategic risks, here are a few things you can try:
Set clear, reachable goals that push you just a bit outside your comfort zone. And when you make progress—even if it feels small—celebrate it! Those wins add up and create real momentum.
Ask trusted colleagues or mentors for feedback. Sometimes, another perspective can help you see strengths—and opportunities for growth—that you might have missed.
Practice speaking up about your achievements and your goals, especially in conversations with supervisors or decision-makers. That’s self-advocacy in action.
And if you’re feeling afraid to fail, try reframing it: instead of “What did I do wrong?” ask, “What can I learn from this?”
Another spot where confidence and risk-taking really matter is negotiation.
A lot of women shy away from negotiating for salary, promotions, or resources—maybe out of worry about seeming difficult or ungrateful. But here’s the truth: negotiation is a normal, even expected, part of work life.
If you approach it as a chance to solve problems together, rather than a confrontation, it can feel a whole lot less intimidating.
The key to negotiating well? Preparation.
Do your homework: learn what’s typical in your industry, get clear about what you want, and think ahead about any pushback you might get.
And if you can, practice your negotiation skills in lower-stakes situations first—it’s a great way to build your confidence before those bigger conversations.
In the end, embracing smart risk-taking is about understanding that real growth means stepping into the unknown now and then.
When you develop the confidence to try new things, speak up for what you need, and learn from the bumps along the way, you’ll start to break through your own limits—and open up a path to even greater success at work.
